speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic. I understand you are having difficulty conceiving and experiencing discomfort during sexual activity; to help you, could you describe exactly where you feel the pain and when this started? Also, have you tried to conceive for more than a year, or are you a woman over 35?

speaker: Patient
text: 30-year-old female. The patient and her husband have been trying to conceive for 15 months without success. They are sexually active at least twice a week. The husband occasionally has difficulties maintaining an erection. The patient reports discomfort and pelvic floor muscle tension during attempted vaginal penetration. Diagnosed with body dysmorphic disorder three years ago. No family history of serious illness. She is a non-smoker and does not drink alcohol. No medications.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Dyspareunia secondary to pelvic floor muscle tension (likely vaginismus) with concurrent male erectile dysfunction. Given the 15-month infertility and specific history of pelvic discomfort, we must rule out structural or inflammatory causes. REQUEST TEST: Pelvic_Ultrasound, REQUEST TEST: Seminal_Analysis.
